level: product registration of the versioned container-command Task backend (design gate 5 of the command facade plan)
componentAcceptance: the remote-command backend is composed into the product task service, plan-execution accepts the command shape, and the product UI renders command receipts truthfully
productAcceptance: partial; the Docker success path runs through the component suite on real machines, while a full product-boot end-to-end command scenario (combined-host with a live container) remains with the combined-host acceptance runs
implementation: product-composition composes createRemoteCommandBackend beside the remote-write backend and publishes both catalog entries (the command entry is labelled alias-argv only); the task service therefore accepts backend remote-command from Bot Task submissions with the same journal, admission and reconciliation machinery

parseTaskPlan accepts workspace-write plans whose package execution is {backend:'remote-command', input:{machineId,rootId,workspaceRelativePath,argv,timeoutMs}} — the normalized plan preserves the actual backend and re-validates with the command parser; read-effect, cross-backend and malformed inputs are refused
the product task projection carries command receipt fields additively: exitCode when integral and notStarted when true, next to the existing sha256/bytes write fields

the model-facing bot_task_plan_start description documents the command execution shape with its boundary (operator-approved argv alias, container-only, no paths/endpoints/secrets, never a native shell)
the published-files manifest gained the new module — caught by the closure test, not by hand

platforms.tests: 21/21 pass, 0 fail (8 command incl. the plan case and real-container dispatch, 8 UI receipt incl. the two new command cases, 5 contract)
21 tests, 16 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (Docker-gated dispatch cases)

platforms.rootRegression: 1853 tests, 1785 pass, 0 fail, 68 skipped, exit 0 (log: tmp/integration/command-product-registration-root.log); check:client OK

preservedFailures: Development findings, reproduced and fixed: the plan parser had a second hard-coded remote-write site in its normalized return (the stack trace exposed it); one parenthesis slip in the same edit broke compilation; a bad-case assertion needed the INVALID_TASK_REQUEST code; and the published-file-list closure test caught the unregistered new module. The first full regression failed 2 items on these; all were fixed and the regression rerun to 0 failures.
limitations: The product-boot end-to-end command scenario (combined-host with a live container) still rides on the existing combined-host runs, which do not yet include a command case; adding one is follow-up acceptance work.
Model-facing exposure remains effect-gated (workspace-write plans and write/command grants); opening command tools to broader model use is a separate policy decision.
Windows OS-boundary commands, slices 4/5 of the stop fence and real inference/billing acceptance remain open.
